sections.h2: Where is Casselberry and why does location matter when selling?
sections.html:
Casselberry sits in the southern end of Seminole County, about ten miles north of downtown Orlando, according to the city. That position is the first thing many buyers weigh.

The city's general information page says the airport in Orlando is roughly 30 minutes away and Orlando Sanford International about 15 minutes. Interstate 4 is five minutes from the city, and State Road 436 and U.S. 17-92 cross inside it. The Lynx bus system serves local routes. For a house here, commute time and road access are legitimate selling points to put in front of a buyer.

The city covers approximately 8 square miles, so most neighborhoods are small and close together. Seminole County, not the city, assesses, bills and records property, which keeps the paperwork simple.

sections.h2: What do the lakes, parks and schools add to a Casselberry house?
sections.html:
The city counts more than two dozen lakes and 18 parks within its limits. The largest lakes are Lake Howell, Lake Kathryn and the Triplet Chain of Lakes, which includes North, South and Middle Lake Triplet.

The same page names Casselberry Elementary and South Seminole Middle School as public schools inside the city, plus two private schools, Lake Forrest Preparatory School and The Geneva School. Buyers with children often check school boundaries with Seminole County Public Schools, so confirm attendance zones for your address instead of promising one.

  • Lake and park proximity: mention the nearest water body by name in your listing.
  • Retail and offices: the city lists a mix of shops, restaurants and commercial space near residential streets.
  • Library: the Central Branch of the Seminole County Library is inside the city.

The city's page also describes Casselberry as a Commission and City Manager government. Population and income figures on that page date from 2018 and the 2010 census, so use current Census Bureau data when you need a number.

sections.h2: What dates does the Seminole County Property Appraiser publish?
sections.html:
The office keeps a short list of recurring dates that every Casselberry owner should know.

Seminole County Property Appraiser, important dates
DateEvent
January 1Date of assessment for all property
March 1Deadline to apply for homestead exemption or agricultural classification
April 1Deadline for personal property returns
Mid-AugustProposed tax (TRIM) notices mailed
25 days after mailingDeadline for real property petitions to the Value Adjustment Board
NovemberValue Adjustment Board hearings begin; Tax Collector mails bills

The office's home page notes that January 1 through March 1 is the regular filing window for the current tax year, and that filing between March 2 and December 31 counts as pre-filing for the next year.

sections.h2: How does Casselberry's tax bill get paid, and when is it late?
sections.html:
The county's Tax Collector mails bills in November and offers a sliding discount: 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. Nothing is discounted in March, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1.

Florida also allows installment prepayment with an application to the tax collector by May 1, and partial payments may be accepted at the collector's discretion before delinquency. Ask the Seminole County Tax Collector how those options work for your parcel.

Before listing, confirm the status of each year's bill. A buyer's title agent will, and surprises cost time.

sections.h2: Can I move a house into a trust or use a lady bird deed before selling?
sections.html:
You can, but the tax effects deserve a conversation with an attorney. A revenue advisement says a lady bird deed, as described in the facts it reviewed, transfers no present beneficial interest and so carries no documentary stamp tax. It is one advisement on one set of facts, not a rule for every deed.

The same agency adds that there is no specific exemption for deeds that move Florida real property for estate planning. Quit claim deeds and contracts for deed are on its list of taxable documents. A transfer of title is generally a change of ownership for Save Our Homes purposes unless an exception applies, such as a transfer between spouses.

If a family member's name needs to come off title before a sale, expect the same signing rule as any conveyance: writing, with two subscribing witnesses under section 689.01.

sections.h2: How much has the Save Our Homes cap allowed lately?
sections.html:
The state's cap chart, revised in January 2026, shows a 2024 inflation figure of 3.4 percent with a cap of 3.0 percent, a 2025 figure of 2.9 percent with a cap of 2.9 percent, and a 2026 figure of 2.7 percent with a cap of 2.7 percent. The cap is the lower of 3 percent or the inflation change, so assessed value on a long-held Casselberry homestead rises slowly while market value may climb faster.

That gap is the savings a seller carries. When the house sells, the buyer's assessment resets to just value, and the seller who buys again in Florida may move part of the gap through portability. File the portability form with the homestead application on the new property by March 1, and make the new home your permanent residence by January 1.

  • Gather your last three tax bills to see how the assessed and just values compare.
  • Confirm that the homestead exemption is still active on the latest roll.
  • Keep a copy of the portability form with your closing file.

sections.h2: What should a Casselberry seller do in the weeks before closing?
sections.html:
Work through a short checklist so each Seminole County office has what it needs. The title agent normally runs most of it, but you speed things up by having documents ready.

  • Order a payoff from your lender and ask whether a prepayment charge applies.
  • Check the city for open permits on additions, sheds or roof work.
  • Confirm that every owner on title can sign, or that a legal representative has authority.
  • Ask the title agent how the November tax bill will be split at closing.
  • Cancel or transfer water, sewer and garbage service, which the city provides as municipal utilities.

Once the deed is signed it goes to the county clerk for recording, and the new owner files for their own exemption by the following March 1.

sections.h2: What about tenants and inherited or distressed houses in Casselberry?
sections.html:
For a rented house, the notice depends on the problem. Nonpayment needs 3 days' written notice that skips weekends and court holidays. A curable lease violation gives the tenant 7 days to cure, and an incurable one gives 7 days to vacate. After a landlord wins in court the sheriff gives 24 hours' posted notice before restoring possession.

Inherited houses usually need probate authority first. Summary administration is available when the non-exempt estate does not exceed $150,000 or the owner has been dead more than 2 years. Florida levies no estate tax for deaths after 2004.

If the owner is behind on the mortgage, a foreclosure sale follows judgment by 20 to 35 days, and the high bidder posts 5 percent. Selling earlier gives you more say in the terms.

faqs.a: Yes. The city describes itself as the southernmost community in Seminole County, about ten miles north of downtown Orlando. The county offices handle your assessment, tax bill and recording.

faqs.q: When do I apply for homestead in Seminole County?
faqs.a: By March 1. The Property Appraiser says January 1 to March 1 is the regular window, and applications between March 2 and December 31 are pre-filing for the next year.

faqs.q: What discount applies if I pay early?
faqs.a: 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, per the Property Appraiser. March carries no discount and April 1 begins delinquency.

faqs.q: Does a lady bird deed avoid the deed tax?
faqs.a: Not always. The state agency reached that result on one set of facts where the owners kept full powers, so get an attorney's read on yours.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest my Casselberry value?
faqs.a: 25 days after the mid-August TRIM mailing. The notice itself states the filing deadline.
